theme: LLM coders below reliability target (no human ground truth)
response: Replaced the same-vendor adjudication design with independent OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google judges and deterministic aggregation. Nominal alpha=0.471 remains below gate, so R2 is secondary/descriptive. Majority, strict, unanimous, leave-one-out, pairwise, and preselected repeatability results plus all raw evidence-grounded judgments are released. No gold-standard or human-reliability claim is made.

theme: Same-vendor model family -> correlated blind spots
response: The final panel uses three independently operated providers. Limitations still acknowledges correlated training-data and convention blind spots; inter-model agreement is not presented as correctness or human reliability.

First-pass (5/26) and repaired (7/26) endpoints are reported SEPARATELY throughout, never merged; every patch released; Limitations states a different auditor could move at most the two repaired cases. This is the preregistered separation-of-unassisted-and-repaired-execution design, not a post-hoc fix.

theme: Small N=26, sparse category cells, OR=10.3 may be over-read
response: All category comparisons and the R2-E3 association are explicitly labeled exploratory with non-significant p-values reported inline; Limitations warns against generalizing category proportions. New family-lineage paragraph adds a pseudo-replication caveat. We report effect sizes + intervals, not significance claims.

theme: Corpus screening single-pass/subjective -> selection bias, A0=A1 saturation
response: Exclusion is framed as inability to resolve the official artifact in this pass, NOT a claim none exists; corpus_excluded.csv (exclusion ledger) and search keywords are released; PRISMA-style counts reported. A0=A1=26/26 is explicitly a property of the INCLUDED corpus, not the candidate pool. Selection effect flagged in Limitations (Scope of resolution).

theme: Contribution is a checklist/audit, not a new dataset/method (niche vs core)
response: Reviewers unanimously judged the survey/checklist objection survivable and novelty clear. Differentiators (frozen-commit repository inspection + controlled zero-inference CPU execution + unassisted/repaired separation) are exactly the two columns no located prior framework fills. This is the Datasets&Benchmarks track's remit (evaluation infrastructure). Recommendations + reusable pipeline are concrete community deliverables.
Table 3 caption now defines R2 crit, R2, E3 fp/rep/E3.
Category cells (n=4-5) are too small for meaningful CIs; text labels them exploratory. Retained as descriptive, per analysis conventions that discourage over-precise small-cell inference.

theme: Claim-evidence concordance is another small-subgroup inference
response: Reported as a descriptive count (2/14) with denominator explicit, not an inferential claim; consistent with exploratory framing.

theme: Nominal vs ordinal alpha reads as metric shopping
response: Results now states nominal alpha is the preregistered primary metric and ordinal/AC1 are post-hoc characterizations, not a re-choice of endpoint.
Matrix coded from each framework's own paper/abstract, stated as such; a common positioning device, disclosed.

theme: Artifact release lacks DOI/link in manuscript text
response: Persistent identifier/DOI to be inserted at camera-ready once the release is minted; review version keeps single-blind neutrality. Availability statement present.

theme: One-decimal percentages overstate precision at N=26
response: Every proportion is paired with a 95% CI showing the true precision; one-decimal reporting kept for table alignment and to match k/n exactly. CIs are the precision signal, not the point estimate.

theme: Missing comparison to ACM/IEEE artifact-evaluation badges
response: Artifact-badging does per-paper reviewer-run checks but not systematic cross-benchmark, claim-evidence-concordance auditing of the evaluation specification; a one-line contrast could be added but does not change positioning.
